$comment: THE GOLDEN TALLY. This file is the machine-readable original of the worked
seeded-defect tally printed in docs/PROCESS.md §3.9. The document's figures are
DERIVED FROM THIS FILE and must not be edited in the document alone.
Why it exists: the sixth edition's §3.9 carried a prose copy of the constitution's
two-column law and dropped the clause that made it determinate, so a cold reader
could produce two different tallies from one record (council round 5, Charlie F1 /
Outsider 1 / Bill F9 / Contrarian 3). A rule stated only in prose drifts; a rule
with a committed worked instance beside it cannot drift silently, because the
instance stops closing. This file is that instance in the form a script can read.
It carries THIS program's real identifiers. docs/PROCESS.md is de-domained and
prints an anonymized rendering of the same numbers; docs/PROCESS-MEMOIR.md Annex C
is the name map between them. A fork deletes this file whole and writes its own
The invariant a checker must enforce: sealed = seeded + |difference|, and
seeded = killed + survived + green_by_blindness. Both close below.

derived_at.note: Figures re-derived from the committed record in the act that printed them, never quoted from the previous printing.

law.sealed: every defect class the manifest sealed, with nothing removed from it for any later reason
law.seeded: the subset rendered against the artefact AS SEALED and run; the gate clause is read against this column
law.determinacy_clause: All three sit in `sealed`, none in `seeded`, each named at the tally with its ground.
law.grounds_are_open: A class excluded on any ground is named at the tally with it, where the gate reads that ground and may refuse it.
law.disclosure_rule: A ground that turns on what the seal disclosed — grounds 2 and 3 — holds only where the disclosure was frozen in the seal BEFORE the run, never on what the run returned.
law.unit: the defect class, not the branch, ref or file that delivered it

outside_this_tally.note: Scored in a different unit (the mutation, not the class). A single ratio over all fourteen campaigns does not exist and is not manufactured here.

rehabilitation.form: the strict one: the UNMODIFIED committed diff replayed against the bench as it stands, at a run id, with the killing unit named

seeded_non_kills_itemised.two_facts_never_folded: the campaign's own `survived` count keeps what it measured; the defect is measured dead at the run id above. Neither sentence may be quoted without the other.
seeded_non_kills_itemised.expiry_condition: a rehabilitation is good only at the state it was taken at. The bench has since moved by nearly twenty thousand added lines across forty-five files; the patch still applies, so the repair costs a single run — but citing this run id after the patch stops applying is the same defect wearing the approved form.

unreachable_set.$comment: Published BESIDE the tally, never inside it. A check no possible defect of the artefact could reach discharges its requirement row like any other and contributes NOTHING to a coverage claim — counting it counts one observation twice. A check the seeded set merely happened not to reach is a seeding gap and may not be entered here.

declared_non_asserting.note: This is NOT an unreachable check: a row with no assertion and a check no defect can reach are different objects, and folding them would put an undischarged row inside a set that discharges.

per_campaign.$comment: sealed_by_manifest is what the manifest sealed. sealed_in_era_figure is what the era's own carried figure counted, which removed two non-scoring classes from the denominator under the pre-amendment reading. The difference between the two columns is the 63 → 65 movement the sign-off itself names and routes as owed to its carrier: a definition change with no measurement behind it.

carried_era_figure.$comment: What the record's own sign-off packet carries, quoted rather than restated, so that this file never silently replaces a committed measurement.
carried_era_figure.source: agents/handoffs/SO-xgmii_rx_64.md §2.2 and §2.2-M, walked at 2183d71 over the campaign verdicts; ceiling of 61 fixed before the last campaign ran (WO-0077 §14) and reached exactly
carried_era_figure.why_it_differs_from_sealed_65: The era figure counted IC-M5 inside `sealed` (as its `void` column) while removing I-c1 and IC-2 from the denominator entirely. Under the amended definition — nothing removed from `sealed` for any later reason — all three sit in `sealed` and none in `seeded`. The sign-off names this movement itself (§2.2-D.6 item 4: 'the movement (b.1) will make to the sealed figure (63 → 65) — a definition change with no measurement behind it, which lands on its own carrier and must say so in the same sentence'). This file is that carrier. NO MEASUREMENT MOVED: the killed, survived and green-by-blindness columns are unchanged, and every campaign score is quoted from its own committed verdict, unedited.
carried_era_figure.owed: The sign-off packet's own re-statement of its SC-5 cell at the amended definition. Owner: the verification lead. Not performed here — this file is the document's derivation source, not the gate record.

what_this_file_does_not_do: It does not re-run, re-score or rehabilitate anything. Every campaign score is quoted from its own committed verdict and stands unedited, including the falsified seal cells.

It does not measure GREEN. The gate clause asks for each named killing unit present AND green at the gate SHA; presence is measured in SO-xgmii_rx_64.md §2.2-D.4, green is CI's verdict at a gate SHA that does not yet exist.
It does not form a ratio, and no reader may form one from it. Five columns exist precisely so that a single figure cannot destroy the fourth and fifth.
It does not cover the pre-class era's four campaigns, which are scored in a different unit and stated separately above.
